unread.text: Build and deploy a webhook receiver for our payment provider's event notifications.
Accept HTTP callbacks from the provider at a public endpoint.
Establish that each callback genuinely came from the provider before acting on it.
Keep every callback received, so that a chargeback dispute raised weeks later can be settled by what we actually received at the time.
Let our support team look up past callbacks by the provider's event id.
Expose a health endpoint for the load balancer.
Only our support team should be able to read past callbacks.
The provider is the only party that should be able to submit them.

retention: RDS store "webhook" holds the records and can be destroyed — no deletion_protection = true, or lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }. Nothing here expires these records, but one `terraform destroy`, or one resource replacement, ends the 7 year(s) the task requires. Declaring protection on some other resource does not count: a deliverable set enable_deletion_protection on its load balancer while the database holding the callbacks had none.

code quality: none of the 3 test file(s) import anything from this project — tests/duplicate-handling.test.js, tests/runner.js, tests/signature-verification.test.js. A test that never reaches the code under test cannot be evidence about it, however many assertions it contains and whether or not it passes: asserting that two identical HMAC calls agree tests the crypto library, and asserting that a string copied from a source file contains a substring tests the copy. Import the modules being tested and exercise them.

advisories.message: authentication: 1 route(s) exempt by name, not checked — GET /health (src/index.js:26, probe). Probe paths (/health, /ping, /metrics and the like) are expected to be open, and an endpoint that issues a credential cannot require it first. The exemption is by path alone: a route with one of these names that reads request input or changes state needs authentication like any other.
secret rotation: the task says a secret rotates, but nothing here reads a secret from a managed store — a secret delivered another way cannot pick up a rotation without a restart

retention: backup_retention_period is set, and it is not record retention. A backup window is how far back the store can be restored — at most 35 days on RDS and DynamoDB — not how long a record survives inside it. The task asks for 7 year(s). Nothing here deletes the records, so the requirement is not violated, but nothing here establishes it either.

code quality: 3 test file(s) found and read — tests/duplicate-handling.test.js, tests/runner.js, tests/signature-verification.test.js. This is what is in the files, not what happens when they run; the tests check reports that separately, and its verdict is the one that counts. A test that imports a module before setting the environment that module reads, or patches an attribute it does not have, looks entirely reasonable in the file and fails the moment it runs.
